title: Prove It Still Works: A Self-Test That Runs Every Check, a Permit That Expires, and the Stop That Cannot Be Tested From Software Alone

questions.question: Why must safety functions be tested on purpose?
options: They are used so often that they wear out
Regulations ask for a signature each week
They are dormant: a welded relay or a cut wire gives no sign until the moment the function is needed
They slow the control loop if left untested
questions.explanation: A function that is only needed in an emergency can be broken for months without anyone knowing. Testing it is the only way to find out before it is needed.

questions.question: Five checks run, and the second fails. Does the run stop?
options: No: every check is run and every failure reported (three failed in the test), and a throw or a missing check is a failure too
Yes, at the first failure, to save time
Yes, but the failure is logged
Only if the failure was an exception
questions.explanation: Stopping at the first failure hides the others. All five ran, three failed, and a check that threw or was missing counted as a failure too.

questions.question: What does all_passed give for an empty list of results?
options: true: nothing failed
An error, since there is nothing to judge
Whatever the last run gave
false: a test that checked nothing has not passed
questions.explanation: A self test that somebody emptied, or whose checks never registered, would otherwise report a perfect result.

questions.question: With the contactor welded closed, which check failed?
options: Both: a welded contactor fails every check
Neither: the software cannot see a weld
Only the one that read the contactor: the software check passed, because the software was right and the machine could not stop
The software check only
questions.explanation: The stop logic did command the supply open, so the check of the logic passed. Only reading the contactor's auxiliary contact showed that it had not opened.

questions.question: A test that passed an hour ago, and one that failed a minute ago. Is driving permitted?
options: No: a failed test cancels the earlier pass
Yes: the pass is still within its hour
Yes, at reduced speed
Yes, until the next scheduled test
questions.explanation: The permit comes from the most recent result. A failure a minute ago says more about the machine now than a pass an hour ago.

questions.question: At a failure rate of 1e-5 per hour, how often to test to keep the chance of an undetected failure at 1 in 1000?
options: Every hour
About every 100 hours, 4.2 days: the interval follows from a rate and a target
Once a year
Every 1001 hours
questions.explanation: With a constant rate the chance of having failed by time t is one less e to the minus rate times t. For 1 in 1000 at 1e-5 an hour that is 100.1 hours.
